historical_family.participial_analysis: Merrill classifies verbal -ameke as adjectivizer/nominalizer [participial] and uses cotschimé-ameke < cotschimé ‘dormir’ as its explicit example.

modern_src02.participial_evidence_type: source-note-attested; no independent headword located in current SRC-02

independent_comparative_support.source: Hill, Kenneth C. 2020. Wick Miller's Uto-Aztecan Cognate Sets. UC Berkeley, Survey of California and Other Indian Languages, Report 18.
independent_comparative_support.significance: Modern Rarámuri Cochí belongs to an independently assembled Uto-Aztecan sleep cognate set.

participial_correspondence.historical: cotschimé + participial -ameke; Merrill additionally analyzes historical participial -(a)me plus optional -kV/-ke in relevant chains
participial_correspondence.modern: Cochí -> source-explicit pp. cochíami in SRC-02

comparison_model.unresolved_historical_material: The -mé of historical cotschimé is not assigned a suffixal function here. Merrill groups the forms under COTSCHI- but does not, in the passages audited, analyze -mé as a suffix of this verb.
comparison_model.important_distinction: The candidate now has strong evidence for continuity of the lexical family core koči- and for participial function at both chronological endpoints; the exact historical pathway of cotschimé versus modern Cochí still requires morphological and dialectological explanation.

why_strengthened: Merrill internally groups the historical forms as the COTSCHI- family.
Merrill's phonetic appendix normalizes historical cotschi as koči, aligning the relevant consonant sequence with modern cochí rather than relying on naive orthographic comparison.
Hill independently places modern Rarámuri cochí in Uto-Aztecan cognate set ko-02 ‘sleep’.
Historical and modern evidence both explicitly identify a participial derivative in the same sleep domain.
remaining_tests: Determine the historical/morphological status of -mé in cotschimé from independent Rarámuri descriptions and older sources.
Check whether modern varieties preserve extended stems cognate with historical kočimé or related alternations.
Compare the participial form across multiple modern varieties, not only SRC-02 and Choguita-level general morphology.
Do not infer direct cognacy of the full words until the -mé issue and dialect chronology are resolved.
